card.hook: Atrani packs a beach, an arcade, a pile of pastel houses and a church dome into one frame, which is quite the flex for such a tiny village. Skip the sand, though. The best picture is one flight of steps up.
card.stand_here: Stand on Via Gabriele di Benedetto, the stretch beside the Amalfi Drive road, one flight of steps up from the beach. Face north-west and look down over the beach and arcade, with the church dome showing above the houses.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get the whole scene of beach, arcade and village. Then try zoom 2x or higher (higher zooms depend on your phone) to pick out the church dome and the colours of the houses.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the church or the front of the houses, then drag the brighter/darker slider down a little so the sky doesn't wash out.
card.best_time: Blue hour, when the village lights come on, is the time a guide recommends for the best light. If it's getting dark, switch on night mode and hold your phone as still as you can.
card.selfie_here: Head to the terrace of the Collegiate Church of Santa Maria Maddalena, down the stairs from the church square, with the sea in front of you and the village behind. Use the front camera, try 0.5x to fit more in, and keep the village over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand at the far end of the breakwater on Atrani beach and look back toward the town, while you stand in front of them so the beach and village are in the frame.
card.rules_and_safety: Take care when you stop beside the road, because the Amalfi Drive has narrow stretches without pavements. Conditions can change, so check locally.
card.challenge: Get the beach on the lower gridline and the dome on an upper crossing point, with no leaning houses. Bonus points if you can spot the arcade too.
card.good_to_know: Atrani is officially the smallest municipality in Italy, covering just 12 hectares, with about 832 people living here in 2020. Long ago it was the twin of Amalfi, and the dukes of Amalfi were crowned in the chapel of San Salvatore, wearing a cap called the "birecto". The old central square opens onto the beach through a passageway built to save boats from sea storms.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Via Gabriele di Benedetto, the stretch beside the Amalfi Drive road, one flight of steps up from the beach. Face north-west and look down over the beach and arcade, with the church dome showing above the houses.

card.hook: Picture a stack of postcards sliding into one shot: bobbing boats, a curve of harbour, pastel houses, then a steep hillside piled on top. That's Marina Grande, and it's a layer cake worth framing.
card.stand_here: Stand by Amalfi's harbour and beach front, and face south-west toward the marina. Then build your shot from the layers in front of you: boats, harbour, houses, hillside.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get the marina and its surroundings together. Go to 0.5x for more hillside and sea, or 2x-5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the boats and the beach umbrellas.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on gridlines, put the harbour edge on the lower line, and let the houses fill the middle with sky above, keeping the horizon level.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning, before it gets hot. It's more comfortable, and it's also the best time for the optional walk up to the belvedere.
card.selfie_here: Walk to the end of the middle quay of the harbour, then use the front camera at 0.5x so both sides of Amalfi and the harbour fit behind you. For a bigger view, climb one of the terraces or the switchback lanes above the harbour so the curve of the bay and the pastel buildings are over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the walkway beside the beach and shoot down, while you stand on the sand in front of the teal and yellow umbrellas so the beach and harbour show behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: If you stroll up toward the cemetery, keep to the side of the path so others can pass, and check the official site for any visiting rules at the cemetery itself.
card.challenge: Can you get all four layers (boats, harbour, houses, hillside) in one frame without a stray bag or sign sneaking in at the edge?
card.good_to_know: Marina Grande is Amalfi's harbour and beach front, with pastel buildings and steep cliffs rising straight behind it. The small beach with its teal and yellow umbrellas gives you a bright splash of colour at water level. If you want a quieter, wider view, the Belvedere Cimitero Monumentale on the walk toward the cemetery shows more of the whole town than the marina, so treat it as an optional extra.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the phone icon on the map, by Amalfi's harbour and beach front, and face south-west toward the marina. Then build your shot from the layers in front of you: boats, harbour, houses, hillside.

selfie_spots.why: The quay's end gives a view across both sides of Amalfi, so the harbour sits behind you in a wide frame.

card.hook: There are 62 wide, steep steps between you and Amalfi's front door, and they make the best frame in town. The striped facade above them looks like a postcard because, well, it's the standard postcard view.
card.stand_here: Stand in Piazza Duomo at the foot of the cathedral steps, facing up toward the facade. From Piazza del Duomo it's about 1 minute on foot to the cathedral itself.
card.zoom: Start at 0.5x to fit the facade, bell tower and steps into one shot. Switch to 1x for a more natural look, then try 2x or more (depends on your phone) to pick out the mosaics at the top and the tiled crown of the tower.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the facade, then slide to darker just a touch so the bright marble and mosaics keep their detail.
card.best_time: Go in late afternoon, when the sun lights up the mosaics and the facade. In a busy square, take a few shots in a row and keep the one with the clearest foreground.
card.selfie_here: Climb to one of the triple-arched windows beside the stairs and pose inside its frame. The shade of the atrium against the sunlight outside makes a lovely contrast, so use the front camera and tap your face so you don't turn dark.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand directly in front of the cathedral at the bottom of the steps while you stand up on the stairs, so the whole facade fits behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: The 62 steps are wide and steep, and on a hot summer day you might need a break on the way up. The cathedral is a place of worship, so check the official site for visiting times, dress code and any ticket for the interior.
card.challenge: Zoom to 2x or more and find the mosaic at the top of the facade, then pull right back to 0.5x and see if you can squeeze in all 62 steps too.
card.good_to_know: The facade is fairly young: part of the earlier front collapsed in 1861, and the rebuilt Arab-Norman and Gothic face was finished in 1891. The bell tower was begun in 1180 and finished over a century later, and its little towers are covered in bright majolica tiles. The bronze doors are older still, cast in Constantinople before 1066.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Piazza Duomo at the foot of the cathedral steps, facing up toward the facade. From Piazza del Duomo it's about 1 minute on foot to the cathedral itself.

card.hook: Here's a fun one: a museum all about paper, and the best photo is of its front door. It's a calm, quick stop where a sign or doorway says exactly where you've been.
card.stand_here: Stand right at the phone icon on the map, which sits at the Museo della Carta itself, so there's no viewpoint to hunt for. Face the front of the building, find the cleanest view, and step back if other visitors are in the way.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for a natural view of the entrance. If the street is too narrow to fit the building in, try 0.5x and keep your phone level so the walls don't lean. Use 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) for signs and little details.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines and line the doorway up with the vertical lines so the building stands up straight.
card.best_time: Go when the street is quiet so fewer people wander into your frame. Soft daylight flatters a building front much more than harsh midday sun.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x to fit more behind you, and keep the building's front over your shoulder. Check the view when you arrive and shuffle left or right until the entrance is in the frame.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on Via delle Cartiere, on the street outside the museum entrance, while you stand at the entrance itself.
card.rules_and_safety: Photography is permitted in most areas inside, but check for restrictions when you arrive, and avoid flash where you can. The historic building has uneven stone floors and steps, so watch your feet while you frame your shot.
card.challenge: Take two shots: one wide picture of the whole entrance and one close-up of a sign or detail, then pick your favourite for the travel diary.
card.good_to_know: The Museo della Carta is Amalfi's paper museum, and the name means exactly that. It's rank 4 on this map. Check the official site before you go for opening arrangements, tickets and any rules about photography inside.

card.hook: Your legs will complain about the steps long before your camera roll does, but this round stone tower on a hilltop is worth every one. Amalfi, Atrani and the sea are laid out below it like a model village.
card.stand_here: Stand on the Veliero del Belvedere terrace, on the trail branch just before the tower, on the uphill side. Face out over the coast and towns, with Torre dello Ziro in the background.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the coast-and-towns view. Go 0.5x to squeeze in more slope and sea, or 2x to 5x (depends on your phone) to pull the tower closer.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on gridlines, put the horizon on the top or bottom line so the coast doesn't look tilted, and park the tower on a third so it doesn't take over.
card.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light usually flatters the coast best. Leave enough daylight to get back down all those steps, since the round trip from Pontone takes roughly 1.5 to 2.5 hours.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera on the Veliero del Belvedere terrace and keep the tower over your shoulder. There's also a higher belvedere a short climb above the tower, which reviewers say frames the tower and coastline well for posing, but ask locally to find it.
card.ask_someone: In Piazza Duomo in Amalfi, hand your phone to a passer-by, stand in the square, and ask them to frame you with the tower visible above the rooftops (check the tower really shows in the shot).
card.rules_and_safety: Treat the tower as a ruin and photograph it from outside, as going in may not be safe. Check on the day and take care near edges.
card.challenge: Walk up to the tower and catch all three layers in one shot: tower in front, Amalfi and Atrani in the middle, sea at the back.
card.good_to_know: Torre dello Ziro is a cylindrical ruined tower on a hilltop above Amalfi and Atrani. Most walkers set out from Pontone, in Scala, and the trail has plenty of steps. Use a hiking app or an offline map, because Google Maps routing has been reported as wrong here.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the Veliero del Belvedere terrace, on the trail branch just before the tower, on the uphill side. Face out over the coast and towns, with Torre dello Ziro in the background.

card.hook: Picture a wedding party posing on a staircase of about 62 steps, with a striped cathedral rising behind them. That's Amalfi's Piazza Duomo on a good day, and it's the classic first photo stop in town.
card.stand_here: Stand in Piazza Duomo at the foot of the cathedral steps and face east towards the striped facade. Put the fountain low in your frame and let the steps lead the eye upward.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for a natural view of the facade. If the steps and fountain won't both fit, tap 0.5x. Then try 2x to 5x (depends on your phone) to pick out the mosaics.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on your gridlines and keep the phone level, so the tall facade doesn't lean backwards.
card.best_time: Aim for late afternoon, when the light falls on the cathedral's mosaics. The steps get busy with tourists and wedding parties, so take a few shots as people move and you'll get a clear one.
card.selfie_here: Climb the Duomo steps, turn so the facade is behind you, and use the front camera. Guides say arriving early keeps the steps clear of other visitors. For a second option, stand beside the Fountain of Sant'Andrea, which sits opposite the cathedral, so the facade is behind you.
card.ask_someone: Stand on the steps with the facade behind you and ask a passer-by to stand at the foot of the staircase and shoot upward, so the whole facade and steps fit in.
card.rules_and_safety: The square is free to visit, but the cathedral is a place of worship. Its opening hours and mass times can block access to the steps, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Take one wide shot of the whole square, then one close shot of the facade and steps, and see which one you'd frame on your wall.
card.good_to_know: Piazza Duomo is the square in front of Amalfi's cathedral. The cathedral's striped facade rises above a staircase of about 62 steps. It's a short, flat walk from the harbour and the bus stop, which makes it an easy first stop.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Piazza Duomo at the foot of the cathedral steps and face east towards the striped facade. Put the fountain low in your frame and let the steps lead the eye upward.

card.hook: You'll hear the square before you see it: Amalfi's Piazza Duomo is buzzing, and right in the middle sits a fountain with the whole cathedral facade rising up behind it. That pairing is the reason to stop.
card.stand_here: Stand at the Fontana di Sant'Andrea in Piazza Duomo, where the phone icon on the map sits. Face the fountain with the cathedral rising behind it.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x. If the fountain and the facade won't fit together, drop to 0.5x. Use zoom 2x or higher for close shots of the statue.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the fountain on the lower third and the facade across the top, and keep your phone level so the cathedral doesn't lean.
card.best_time: The square is very crowded by day, so expect people in your shot. Be patient, wait a moment for a gap and take a few frames in a row.
card.selfie_here: Stand in Piazza Duomo at the fountain's edge, where visitors come to take selfies. Use the front camera, try 0.5x if your phone has it, and tuck the cathedral in over your shoulder. The exact angle isn't pinned down, so test a couple of shots when you arrive.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the cathedral steps while you stand by the fountain, so they can frame you with the fountain and the cathedral facade behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: Piazza Duomo and the cathedral staircase are open-air and free to stand in. If you want to go inside the cathedral, check the official site first.
card.challenge: Take the same fountain shot three times: close on the statue, then the fountain with the facade, then a wide one from the staircase. Which one is your favourite?
card.good_to_know: The fountain stands in Piazza Duomo, in front of the Cattedrale di Sant'Andrea. Guides say the cathedral staircase is the best photo position, because you see the fountain and the facade together. It's about 62 steps up, so allow a minute and take your time with your phone in hand.

card.hook: Here's a cloister where the arches do half your work for you. Every step puts another row of them in front of you, like a set of ready-made picture frames.
card.stand_here: Stand right on the phone icon, because it's inside the cloister itself. Then turn slowly on the spot, since the best view is often behind you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the arches and the whole courtyard in one frame, which really helps in such a tight space. Switch to 1x for a more natural look, then try 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) for columns, carved capitals and old stone.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on gridlines and line a walkway up with a vertical grid line so the arches run straight, then tap the brightest part of the courtyard and drag the slider down a little so the sunny bits keep their detail.
card.best_time: Earlier or later in the day usually means fewer people and softer light in the courtyard, and morning light through the arches is a favourite. At midday the sun makes harsh contrast between the walkways and the open space, so drag the slider darker if you're there then.
card.selfie_here: Stand in the garden courtyard with the white arches and columns behind you, facing the small central garden. Use the front camera at 0.5x so the arches and the flowers both squeeze in over your shoulder.
card.rules_and_safety: This may be a ticketed or managed site, so check the official site before you go for access details and any rules on photography.
card.challenge: Get one shot straight down a walkway with the arches shrinking away, and wait for a stranger to stroll into the frame so it feels properly grand.
card.good_to_know: The Chiostro del Paradiso is a cloister in the old centre of Amalfi. It's an enclosed courtyard with covered walkways round the edge. Those repeating arches are what make it so good for photos.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand right on the phone icon, because it's inside the cloister itself. Then turn slowly on the spot, since the best view is often behind you.

selfie_spots.why: Reviewers describe the white Moorish-style arches and columns and the flowers in the central garden as the most photogenic part of the cloister, and morning light through the arches is recommended.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a specific spot outside the cloister from which a passer-by could photograph a visitor with the whole landmark, so ask_someone_spot is null. No page I found states selfie stick or tripod rules. Sources give three different addresses: Piazza del Duomo (Trip.com), Via Salita Episcopio 5 (Evendo), and Salita Sopra Muro (Yelp); the cloister sits beside the cathedral, left of its porch, per Yelp. Only one selfie spot was supported by the pages found, so the second slot is empty. The Wikimedia coordinates for the cloister (40°38′05″N 14°36′11″E) match the position you supplied.
